items.title: 4. Approval of the Agenda (Action Required) - 1 min

memo.Quick Summary / Abstract: Motion to approve the agenda as submitted or amended.

Public Comment : The Board will limit comments to items on the agenda and will be accepted in person only. Speaker cards are available at the entrance and can be submitted to the secretary before the meeting begins, or you may raise your hand during the meeting to indicate your desire to speak. Speakers will be called when the agenda item is considered. Comments are limited to 3 minutes per speaker per topic, unless otherwise noted.

items.title: 1. Good Beginnings Workshop with California School Boards Association Consultant

memo.Quick Summary / Abstract: The Redwood City School District Governance Team will participate in the Good Beginnings Workshop, a professional development session designed to foster trust and enhance governance team effectiveness. The workshop will focus on building stronger relationships through understanding roles, responsibilities, and the four elements of teamwork: collaboration, communication, commitment, and celebration. This session is especially valuable for onboarding new Board members and strengthening team cohesion.
memo.Financial Impact: No financial impact to the district.
memo.Speaker: Submission for Approval Prepared by: John R. Baker, Ed.D., Superintendent Approved by: John R. Baker, Ed.D., Superintendent

items.title: 2. Planning Discussion for the 2025–26 School Year

memo.Quick Summary / Abstract: This meeting will focus on reviewing priorities and initiating planning for the 2025-26 school year, with an emphasis on academic excellence, equity, and whole-child support.
memo.Summary: The focus of this meeting is to review priorities and begin preparations for the 2025-26 school year. The Redwood City School District (RCSD) remains committed to fostering academic excellence, equity, and whole-child support. This meeting provides an opportunity for RCSD leadership to reflect on current initiatives, evaluate progress, and make adjustments to meet evolving student and community needs. District planning efforts will include a review of relevant data and also the manner of interpreting data, and budget development. The session will cover key operational areas such as academic priorities, instructional initiatives, and alignment with LCAP goals.
memo.Financial Impact: No financial impact to the district at this time.
memo.Speaker: John R. Baker, Superintendent
